articles.title: SJAA Auction Information
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) is hosting its 28th annual astronomical auction and swap meet at Houge Park on Sunday, April 20, 2008. This event offers a chance for beginners to acquire telescopes and for experienced observers to find equipment, while also serving as a fundraiser for the SJAA with a suggested 10% seller donation. The article also provides a calendar of other SJAA activities, including star parties, dark sky weekends, astronomy classes, and general meetings for March, April, and May.

articles.title: DEEP SKY OBSERVING
articles.summary: This document provides a deep-sky observing list for April 2008, specifically for the third quarter to new moon period. It features a curated selection of galaxies, primarily in Ursa Major, Canes Venatici, Leo, and Virgo, listed from north to south. Each entry includes details such as challenge rating, object type, size, magnitude, coordinates, and brief descriptive notes for observers.

articles.title: The Dawning of the Age of Aquarius
articles.summary: Akkana Peck explores the astronomical realities behind common astrological concepts, starting with the discrepancy between her astrological birth sign and her true astronomical birth sign due to Earth's precession. The article then delves into the complex and debated timing of the "Age of Aquarius," explaining how astrological ages are determined by the vernal equinox's movement through zodiacal signs, which are distinct from constellations. It highlights the lack of consensus among astrologers regarding its start and debunks popular misconceptions from culture.

articles.title: Galaxy Seasons
articles.summary: The article "Galaxy Seasons" explains that twice a year, during fall and spring, our view of the night sky points away from the dense plane of the Milky Way, allowing optimal observation of distant galaxies. The fall season is ideal for viewing members of our Local Group, such as the Andromeda Galaxy and M33, while spring provides opportunities to observe the much larger and more distant Virgo Supercluster. The author emphasizes the need for dark skies and appropriate equipment for these deep-sky observations.

articles.title: SJAA 2007 year end statement
articles.summary: The SJAA's 2007 year-end financial statement reports a total of $27,377.74 across various accounts, with most funds invested in four staggered 1-year CD accounts for higher interest. The organization earned $910.84 in interest from CDs last year and expects to earn around $1100 this year, aiming for this interest to eventually cover liability insurance premiums. Excess funds from the checking account will be added to the maturing CDs.

articles.title: SJAA Yosemite Public Star Party 2008
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) is hosting its annual Yosemite Public Star Party on July 4-5 at Glacier Point, Yosemite National Park. Up to 30 participants will receive free admission and camping in exchange for running public stargazing events on Friday and Saturday evenings, requiring at least one scope per two people. The camping facilities are described as rustic, and priority for participation is given to SJAA members.

articles.title: The Star of Bethlehem Revisited
articles.summary: The author recounts observing a dazzling Jupiter-Venus conjunction in 2008, which prompted a reflection on the "Star of Bethlehem." The article explores the theory that the Star of Bethlehem in 2 B.C.E. was a similarly spectacular, but much closer, planetary conjunction of Jupiter and Venus, potentially appearing as a single bright star to the Magi. It references astronomical perspectives on how such an event could have served as the guiding star mentioned in legend.

articles.title: Invisible Spiral Arms
articles.summary: NASA's Galaxy Evolution Explorer (GALEX) has revealed that many nearby spiral galaxies possess "invisible" spiral arms that extend far beyond their visible light boundaries, making some galaxies more than three times larger than previously thought. These extended arms are comprised of hot, young stars that shine brightly in ultraviolet light, which the GALEX telescope is designed to detect. This discovery provides crucial new clues for scientists studying how galaxies form and evolve, particularly concerning bursts of star formation far from galactic centers.

articles.title: Silicon Valley Astronomy Lectures
articles.summary: This document announces a Silicon Valley Astronomy Lecture by Dr. Jill Tarter from the SETI Institute on April 23, 2008, focusing on the search for extraterrestrial intelligence and the new Allen Telescope Array. The lecture is free and open to the public at Foothill College. Additionally, the article includes a "Last 29 days in Astronomy" section highlighting recent space news and a classified ad for a used telescope.

articles.title: Telescope Loaner Program
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) offers a Telescope Loaner Program, allowing members to test various telescope models and technologies before purchasing. The program maintains a changing inventory of scopes for all experience levels, with a list of currently available and soon-to-be-available telescopes provided. The document also includes club officer contacts, staff for the 'SJAA Ephemeris' newsletter, and general club publication details.
